public_domain_references.web: “Therefore, prostitute, hear Yahweh’s word:
public_domain_references.asv: Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of Jehovah:
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Wherefore, O harlot, hear the word of the LORD:
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore, harlot, hear the word of the Lord:

pob.text: Thus says the Lord GOD: Because your bronze was poured out[a], and your nakedness was uncovered in your prostitutions with your lovers, and because of all the idols of your abominations, and because of the blood of your children whom you gave to them[c][b],

spob.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because your bronze was poured out[a], because you exposed your nakedness in acts of prostitution with your lovers, because of all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children, whom you gave to those idols[b],

public_domain_references.bsb: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your wealth and exposed your nakedness in your promiscuity with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children which you gave to them,
public_domain_references.web: ‘The Lord Yahweh says, “Because your filthiness was poured out, and your nakedness uncovered through your prostitution with your lovers; and because of all the idols of your abominations, and for the blood of your children, that you gave to them;
public_domain_references.asv: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Because thy filthiness was poured out, and thy nakedness uncovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers; and because of all the idols of thy abominations, and for the blood of thy children, that thou didst give unto them;
public_domain_references.kjv: Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thy filthiness was poured out, and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers, and with all the idols of thy abominations, and by the blood of thy children, which thou didst give unto them;
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast poured forth thy money, therefore thy shame shall be discovered in thy harlotry with thy lovers, and [with] regard to all the imaginations of thine iniquities, and for the blood of thy children which thou hast given to them.

pob.text: Therefore[a], behold, I am gathering all your lovers with whom you found pleasure, and all whom you loved, along with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you from every side, and I will uncover your nakedness to them[c][b], and they will see all your nakedness.

spob.text: Therefore, I am gathering all your lovers—the ones you took pleasure in—and everyone you loved, along with everyone you hated. I will bring them against you from every side. I will expose your nakedness before them,[a] and they will see you completely naked.

public_domain_references.bsb: therefore I will surely gather all the lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose you before them, and they will see you completely naked.
public_domain_references.web: therefore see, I will gather all your lovers, with whom you have taken pleasure, and all those whom you have loved, with all those whom you have hated. I will even gather them against you on every side, and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness.
public_domain_references.asv: therefore behold, I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, with all them that thou hast hated; I will even gather them against thee on every side, and will uncover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, therefore I will gather all thy lovers, with whom thou hast taken pleasure, and all [them] that thou hast loved, with all [them] that thou hast hated; I will even gather them round about against thee, and will discover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore, behold, I [will] gather all thy lovers with whom thou hast consorted, and all whom thou hast loved, with all whom thou didst hate; and I will gather them against thee round about, and will expose thy wickedness to them, and they shall see all thy shame.

pob.text: And I will judge you with the judgments of women who commit adultery and who shed blood[b][a], and I will give you over to blood in wrath and jealousy.

spob.text: I will judge you as women guilty of adultery and bloodshed are judged. In my wrath and jealousy, I will give you over to bloody punishment.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood; so I will bring upon you the wrath of your bloodshed and jealousy.
public_domain_references.web: I will judge you as women who break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy.
public_domain_references.asv: And I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will bring upon thee the blood of wrath and jealousy.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I will judge thee, as women that break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will give thee blood in fury and jealousy.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will be avenged on thee with the vengeance of an adulteress, and I will bring upon thee blood of fury and jealousy.

pob.text: I will give you into their hand[a], and they will tear down your vaulted chamber and demolish your high places. They will strip you of your clothes, take your beautiful jewelry[b], and leave you naked and bare.

spob.text: I will hand you over to them. They will tear down your vaulted chamber[a] and destroy your shrines on the heights. They will strip off your clothes, take your beautiful jewelry, and leave you naked and bare.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I will deliver you into the hands of your lovers, and they will level your mounds and tear down your lofty shrines. They will strip off your clothes, take your fine jewelry, and leave you naked and bare.
public_domain_references.web: I will also give you into their hand, and they will throw down your vaulted place, and break down your lofty places. They will strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewels. They will leave you naked and bare.
public_domain_references.asv: I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thy vaulted place, and break down thy lofty places; and they shall strip thee of thy clothes, and take thy fair jewels; and they shall leave thee naked and bare.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I will also give thee into their hand, and they shall throw down thine eminent place, and shall break down thy high places: they shall strip thee also of thy clothes, and shall take thy fair jewels, and leave thee naked and bare.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will deliver thee into their hands, and they shall break down thy house of harlotry, and destroy thine high place; and they shall strip thee of thy garments, and shall take thy proud ornaments, and leave thee naked and bare.

pob.text: They will bring up an assembly against you[b][a], and they will stone you and cut you down with their swords.

spob.text: They will call a group together against you. They will stone you and cut you down with their swords.

public_domain_references.bsb: They will bring a mob against you, who will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.
public_domain_references.web: They will also bring up a company against you, and they will stone you with stones, and thrust you through with their swords.
public_domain_references.asv: They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and thrust thee through with their swords.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they shall bring multitudes upon thee, and they shall stone thee with stones, and pierce thee with their swords.

pob.text: They will burn your houses with fire and execute judgments against you before the eyes of many women[a]. I will put a stop to your prostitution[c][b], and you will no longer give payment.

spob.text: They will set your houses on fire and carry out judicial punishments against you in full view of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will no longer give payment for it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then they will burn down your houses and execute judgment against you in the sight of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers.
public_domain_references.web: They will burn your houses with fire, and execute judgments on you in the sight of many women. I will cause you to cease from playing the prostitute, and you will also give no hire any more.
public_domain_references.asv: And they shall burn thy houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women; and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou shalt also give no hire any more.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they shall burn thine houses with fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many women: and I will cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou also shalt give no hire any more.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they shall burn thine houses with fire, and shall execute vengeance on thee in the sight of many women: and I will turn thee back from harlotry, and I will no more give [thee] rewards.

pob.text: So I will satisfy my wrath against you[a], and my jealousy will turn away from you[b]; then I will be quiet and no longer be angry.

spob.text: So I will let my wrath against you run its course, and my jealousy[a] will turn away from you. Then I will be calm and no longer angry.

public_domain_references.bsb: So I will lay to rest My wrath against you, and My jealousy will turn away from you. Then I will be calm and no longer angry.
public_domain_references.web: So I will cause my wrath toward you to rest, and my jealousy will depart from you. I will be quiet, and will not be angry any more.
public_domain_references.asv: So will I cause my wrath toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry.
public_domain_references.kjv: So will I make my fury toward thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry.
public_domain_references.brenton: So will I slacken my fury against thee, and my jealousy shall be removed from thee, and I will rest, and be no more careful [for thee].

pob.text: Because you did not remember the days of your youth[a], but enraged me with all these things, therefore I also have put your way on your own head, declares the Lord GOD, and you have not committed lewdness beyond all your abominations.

spob.text: You did not remember the days of your youth. Instead, you enraged me by doing all these things. Therefore, I have brought the consequences of your conduct down on your own head, declares the Lord Yahweh. And you have not committed sexual depravity beyond all your other detestable acts.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but enraged Me with all these things, I will surely bring your deeds down upon your own head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed this lewdness on top of all your other abominations?
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have raged against me in all these things; therefore, behold, I also will bring your way on your head,” says the Lord Yahweh: “and you shall not commit this lewdness with all your abominations.
public_domain_references.asv: Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast raged against me in all these things; therefore, behold, I also will bring thy way upon thy head, saith the Lord Jehovah: and thou shalt not commit this lewdness with all thine abominations.
public_domain_references.kjv: Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast fretted me in all these [things;] behold, therefore I also will recompense thy way upon [thine] head, saith the Lord GOD: and thou shalt not commit this lewdness above all thine abominations.
public_domain_references.brenton: Because thou didst not remember thine infancy, and thou didst grieve me in all these things; therefore, behold, I have recompensed thy ways upon thine head, saith the Lord: for thus hast thou wrought ungodliness above all thine [other] iniquities.

pob.text: Look[a], everyone who uses proverbs about you will use this proverb, saying, ‘Like mother, like daughter.’

spob.text: Look, anyone who uses a proverb about you will say, “Like mother, like daughter.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Behold, all who speak in proverbs will quote this proverb about you: ‘Like mother, like daughter.’
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb against you, saying, ‘As is the mother, so is her daughter.’
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use [this] proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use [this] proverb against thee, saying, As [is] the mother, [so is] her daughter.
public_domain_references.brenton: These are all the things they have spoken against thee in a proverb, saying,

pob.text: You are the daughter of your mother[a], who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.

spob.text: You are your mother’s daughter, and she loathed her husband and her children. You are a sister of your sisters, and they loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and children. You are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
public_domain_references.web: You are the daughter of your mother, who loathes her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou art the daughter of thy mother, that loatheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children: your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou [art] thy mother’s daughter, that lotheth her husband and her children; and thou [art] the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands and their children: your mother [was] an Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
public_domain_references.brenton: As is the mother, so is thy mother's daughter: thou art she that has rejected her husband and her children; and the sisters of thy sisters have rejected their husbands and their children: your mother was a Chettite, and [your] father an Amorite.

pob.text: Your older sister is Samaria[a], she and her daughters, who dwell to your left; and your younger sister, who dwells to your right, is Sodom and her daughters.

spob.text: Your older sister is Samaria.[a] She and her daughter towns live to your left. Your younger sister is Sodom. She and her daughter towns live to your right.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your older sister was Samaria, who lived with her daughters to your north; and your younger sister was Sodom, who lived with her daughters to your south.
public_domain_references.web: Your elder sister is Samaria, who dwells at your left hand, she and her daughters; and your younger sister, who dwells at your right hand, is Sodom with her daughters.
public_domain_references.asv: And thine elder sister is Samaria, that dwelleth at thy left hand, she and her daughters; and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.
public_domain_references.kjv: And thine elder sister [is] Samaria, she and her daughters that dwell at thy left hand: and thy younger sister, that dwelleth at thy right hand, [is] Sodom and her daughters.
public_domain_references.brenton: Your elder sister who dwells on thy left hand is Samaria, she and her daughters: and thy younger sister, that dwells on thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.

pob.text: Yet you did not walk in their ways or act according to their abominations[a]; as if that were too little[b], you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.

spob.text: You did not merely walk in their ways and commit their abominations. As if their sins were too little for you, you became even more corrupt than they were in everything you did.

public_domain_references.bsb: And you not only walked in their ways and practiced their abominations, but soon you were more depraved than they were.
public_domain_references.web: Yet you have not walked in their ways, nor done their abominations; but soon you were more corrupt than they in all your ways.
public_domain_references.asv: Yet hast thou not walked in their ways, nor done after their abominations; but, as [if that were] a very little [thing], thou wast more corrupt than they in all thy ways.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yet hast thou not walked after their ways, nor done after their abominations: but, as [if that were] a very little [thing], thou wast corrupted more than they in all thy ways.
public_domain_references.brenton: Yet notwithstanding thou hast not walked in their ways, neither hast thou done according to their iniquities within a little, but thou hast exceeded them in all thy ways.

pob.text: As I live[a], declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom, she and her daughters[b], has not done as you and your daughters have done.

spob.text: “As surely as I live,” declares the Lord Yahweh, “your sister Sodom herself and her associated towns[a] have not done as you and your associated towns have done.”

public_domain_references.bsb: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did as you and your daughters have done.
public_domain_references.web: As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “Sodom your sister has not done, she nor her daughters, as you have done, you and your daughters.
public_domain_references.asv: As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters.
public_domain_references.kjv: [As] I live, saith the Lord GOD, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters.
public_domain_references.brenton: [As] I live, saith the Lord, this Sodom and her daughters have not done as thou and thy daughters have done.

pob.text: Look[a], this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and prosperous ease belonged to her and to her daughters[c][b], but she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

spob.text: Look, your sister Sodom was guilty of this: she and her daughter towns[a] were proud, had plenty of food, and lived in secure comfort. But she did not help the poor and needy.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters were arrogant, overfed, and complacent; they did not help the poor and needy.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Behold, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and prosperous ease was in her and in her daughters. She also didn’t strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom: pride, fulness of bread, and prosperous ease was in her and in her daughters; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
public_domain_references.brenton: Moreover this was the sin of thy sister Sodom, pride: she and her daughters lived in pleasure, in fulness of bread [and] in abundance: this belonged to her and her daughters, and they helped not the hand of the poor and needy.

pob.text: They became haughty and committed abomination before me[b][a], so I removed them when I saw it.

spob.text: They grew proud and did something detestable in my sight. So when I saw it, I removed them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Thus they were haughty and committed abominations before Me. Therefore I removed them, as you have seen.
public_domain_references.web: They were arrogant and committed abomination before me. Therefore I took them away when I saw it.
public_domain_references.asv: And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw [good].
public_domain_references.kjv: And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw [good].
public_domain_references.brenton: And they boasted, and wrought iniquities before me: so I cut them off as I saw [fit].

pob.text: And Samaria did not sin half as much as you; you multiplied your abominations more than they[a], and by all your abominations that you committed, you made your sisters appear righteous.

spob.text: Samaria did not sin even half as much as you did. You committed more abominations than your sisters did. Because of all your abominations, you made your sisters look righteous by comparison.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Furthermore, Samaria did not commit half the sins you did. You have multiplied your abominations beyond theirs, and all the abominations you have committed have made your sisters appear righteous.
public_domain_references.web: Samaria hasn’t committed half of your sins; but you have multiplied your abominations more than they, and have justified your sisters by all your abominations which you have done.
public_domain_references.asv: Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters by all thine abominations which thou hast done.
public_domain_references.kjv: Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters in all thine abominations which thou hast done.
public_domain_references.brenton: Also Samaria has not sinned according to half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine iniquities beyond them, and thou hast justified thy sisters in all thine iniquities which thou hast committed.

pob.text: You also[a], bear your disgrace, because you pronounced judgment in favor of your sisters. By your sins in which you acted more abominably than they, they have become more righteous than you. So you too, be ashamed and bear your disgrace[b], because you made your sisters appear righteous.

spob.text: You too must bear your disgrace. Because your sins were even more detestable than your sisters’ sins, you ended up pleading their case for them.[a] Compared with you, they are more righteous. So be ashamed and bear your disgrace, because you made your sisters appear righteous.

public_domain_references.bsb: So now you must bear your disgrace, since you have brought justification for your sisters. For they appear more righteous than you, because your sins were more vile than theirs. So you too must bear your shame and disgrace, since you have made your sisters appear righteous.
public_domain_references.web: You also bear your own shame yourself, in that you have given judgment for your sisters; through your sins that you have committed more abominable than they, they are more righteous than you. Yes, be also confounded, and bear your shame, in that you have justified your sisters.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou also, bear thou thine own shame, in that thou hast given judgment for thy sisters; through thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they, they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou also confounded, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they: they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou confounded also, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou therefore bear thy punishment, for that thou hast corrupted thy sisters by thy sins which thou hast committed beyond them; and thou hast made them [appear] more righteous than thyself: thou therefore be ashamed, and bear thy dishonour, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.

pob.text: And I will restore their fortunes—the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters[a], and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters—and your fortunes among them[b],

spob.text: I will restore the fortunes[a] of Sodom and her daughter towns, and of Samaria and her daughter towns. I will restore your fortunes along with theirs.

public_domain_references.bsb: But I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, as well as Samaria and her daughters. And I will restore you along with them.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“I will reverse their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and the captivity of your captives among them;
public_domain_references.asv: And I will turn again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them;
public_domain_references.kjv: When I shall bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, then [will I bring again] the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them:
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will turn their captivity, [even] the captivity of Sodom and her daughters; and I will turn the captivity of Samaria and her daughters; and I will turn thy captivity in the midst of them:

pob.text: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed because of all that you have done[a], becoming a comfort to them.

spob.text: so that you may carry your disgrace and be ashamed because of everything you have done, as you become a comfort to them.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: So you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you did to comfort them.
public_domain_references.web: that you may bear your own shame, and may be ashamed because of all that you have done, in that you are a comfort to them.
public_domain_references.asv: that thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be ashamed because of all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them.
public_domain_references.kjv: That thou mayest bear thine own shame, and mayest be confounded in all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them.
public_domain_references.brenton: that thou mayest bear thy punishment, and be dishonoured for all that thou hast done in provoking me to anger.

pob.text: And your sisters[a], Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state, and you and your daughters will return to your former state.

spob.text: Sodom, your sister, and her daughters will return to what they were before. Samaria and her daughters will also return to what they were before. And you and your daughters will return to what you were before.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And your sisters, Sodom with her daughters and Samaria with her daughters, will return to their former state. You and your daughters will also return to your former state.
public_domain_references.web: Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former estate; and Samaria and her daughters will return to their former estate; and you and your daughters will return to your former estate.
public_domain_references.asv: And thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate; and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate; and thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate.
public_domain_references.kjv: When thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, then thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate.
public_domain_references.brenton: And thy sister Sodom and her daughters shall be restored as they were at the beginning, and thou and thy daughters shall be restored as ye were at the beginning.

pob.text: Was not Sodom your sister a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride?[a]

spob.text: When you were proud, didn’t you speak of your sister Sodom as a notorious example?[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Did you not treat your sister Sodom as an object of scorn in the day of your pride,
public_domain_references.web: For your sister Sodom was not mentioned by your mouth in the day of your pride,
public_domain_references.asv: For thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride,
public_domain_references.kjv: For thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride,
public_domain_references.brenton: And surely thy sister Sodom was not mentioned by thy mouth in the days of thy pride:

pob.text: before your wickedness was uncovered[a], as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Aram and all those around her, the daughters of the Philistines[c][b], who despise you from every side.

spob.text: before your wickedness was exposed—when the daughters of Aram, all those around her, and the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you from every side, reproached you.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: before your wickedness was uncovered? Even so, you are now scorned by the daughters of Edom and all those around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines—all those around you who despise you.
public_domain_references.web: before your wickedness was uncovered, as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all who are around her, the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you all around.
public_domain_references.asv: before thy wickedness was uncovered, as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, that do despite unto thee round about.
public_domain_references.kjv: Before thy wickedness was discovered, as at the time of [thy] reproach of the daughters of Syria, and all [that are] round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, which despise thee round about.
public_domain_references.brenton: before thy wickedness was discovered, even now thou art the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all that are round about her, [even] of the daughters of the Philistines that compass thee round about.

pob.text: You have borne your lewdness and your abominations[a], declares Yahweh.

spob.text: You yourself have borne your shameless sexual wrongdoing and your detestable acts, declares Yahweh.[a]

pob.text: Then all the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones[a], remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling, sit on the ground, tremble moment by moment[b], and be appalled at you.

They will raise this lament over you:

“How you have perished!

a city people praised,
strong at sea—
she and her inhabitants brought terror
upon all who lived in her.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Tarshish was your merchant because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Tarshish was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches. They traded for your wares with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
public_domain_references.asv: Tarshish was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded for thy wares.
public_domain_references.kjv: Tarshish [was] thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all [kind of] riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded in thy fairs.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Carthaginians were thy merchants because of the abundance of all thy strength; they furnished thy market with silver, and gold, and iron, and tin, and lead.

pob.text: Javan[a], Tubal, and Meshech—they were your traders; they exchanged human lives and articles of bronze for your wares.

spob.text: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They exchanged human lives[a] and bronze goods for the goods you offered.

public_domain_references.bsb: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants. They exchanged slaves and bronze utensils for your merchandise.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your traders. They traded the persons of men and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.
public_domain_references.asv: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were thy traffickers; they traded the persons of men and vessels of brass for thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.kjv: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they [were] thy merchants: they traded the persons of men and vessels of brass in thy market.
public_domain_references.brenton: Greece, both the whole [world], and the adjacent coasts, these traded with thee in the persons of men, and they gave [as] thy merchandise vessels of brass.

pob.text: From Beth-togarmah they traded horses[a], horsemen[b], and mules for your wares.

spob.text: Beth-togarmah traded horses, war horses,[a] and mules in exchange for your goods.

public_domain_references.bsb: The men of Beth-togarmah exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“They of the house of Togarmah traded for your wares with horses, war horses, and mules.
public_domain_references.asv: They of the house of Togarmah traded for thy wares with horses and war-horses and mules.
public_domain_references.kjv: They of the house of Togarmah traded in thy fairs with horses and horsemen and mules.
public_domain_references.brenton: Out of the house of Thogarma horses and horsemen furnished thy market.

pob.text: The sons of Dedan were your merchants[a]. Many coastlands were the market of your hand[c][b]; they brought back ivory tusks and ebony as your payment.

spob.text: The people of Dedan were your merchants. Many coastlands[a] served as your markets. In return, they brought you ivory tusks and ebony as payment.

public_domain_references.bsb: The men of Dedan were your clients; many coastlands were your market; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“The men of Dedan traded with you. Many islands were the market of your hand. They brought you horns of ivory and ebony in exchange.
public_domain_references.asv: The men of Dedan were thy traffickers; many isles were the mart of thy hand: they brought thee in exchange horns of ivory and ebony.
public_domain_references.kjv: The men of Dedan [were] thy merchants; many isles [were] the merchandise of thine hand: they brought thee [for] a present horns of ivory and ebony.
public_domain_references.brenton: The sons of the Rhodians were thy merchants; from the islands they multiplied thy merchandise, [even] elephants' teeth: and to them that came in thou didst return thy prices,

pob.text: Aram traded with you because of your many products[a], giving turquoise, purple, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral[c][b], and rubies for your wares.

spob.text: Aram traded with you because you produced so many goods. They exchanged turquoise,[a] purple material, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral,[b] and rubies[c] for your merchandise.

public_domain_references.bsb: Aram was your customer because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your wares.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Syria was your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiworks. They traded for your wares with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
public_domain_references.asv: Syria was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of thy handiworks: they traded for thy wares with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and rubies.
public_domain_references.kjv: Syria [was] thy merchant by reason of the multitude of the wares of thy making: they occupied in thy fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and agate.
public_domain_references.brenton: [even] men [as] thy merchandise, from the multitude of thy trading [population], myrrh and embroidered works from Tharsis: Ramoth also and Chorchor furnished thy market.

pob.text: Judah and the land of Israel—they were your merchants; they traded for your merchandise with wheat of Minnith[a], pannag, honey, oil, and balm.

spob.text: Judah and the land of Israel did business with you as merchants. They exchanged Minnith wheat, pannag[a], honey, oil, and balm for your goods.

public_domain_references.bsb: Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, cakes and honey, oil and balm for your merchandise.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Judah and the land of Israel were your traders. They traded wheat of Minnith, confections, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
public_domain_references.asv: Judah, and the land of Israel, they were thy traffickers: they traded for thy merchandise wheat of Minnith, and pannag, and honey, and oil, and balm.
public_domain_references.kjv: Judah, and the land of Israel, they [were] thy merchants: they traded in thy market wheat of Minnith, and Pannag, and honey, and oil, and balm.
public_domain_references.brenton: Juda and the children of Israel, these were thy merchants; in the sale of corn and ointments and cassia: and they gave the best honey, and oil, and resin, to thy trading [population].

pob.text: Damascus traded with you because of your many products[a], because of your abundant wealth, with wine of Helbon and white wool.

spob.text: Damascus did business with you because you had so many products and so much wealth. It traded with you in wine from Helbon and white wool.

public_domain_references.bsb: Because of your many products and your great wealth of goods, Damascus traded with you wine from Helbon, wool from Zahar,
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Damascus was your merchant for the multitude of your handiworks by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches, with the wine of Helbon, and white wool.
public_domain_references.asv: Damascus was thy merchant for the multitude of thy handiworks, by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches, with the wine of Helbon, and white wool.
public_domain_references.kjv: Damascus [was] thy merchant in the multitude of the wares of thy making, for the multitude of all riches; in the wine of Helbon, and white wool.
public_domain_references.brenton: [The people of] Damascus were thy merchants by reason of the abundance of all thy power; wine out of Chelbon, and wool from Miletus; and they brought wine into thy market.

pob.text: Dan and Javan from Uzal traded with you[a]; they exchanged wrought iron, cassia[c][b], and cane for your wares.

spob.text: Dan[a] and Javan from Uzal[b] traded with you. In exchange for your goods, they gave you worked iron, cassia spice, and cane.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: and casks of wine from Izal for your wares. Wrought iron, cassia, and sweet cane were exchanged for your merchandise.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Vedan and Javan traded with yarn for your wares; wrought iron, cassia, and calamus were among your merchandise.
public_domain_references.asv: Vedan and Javan traded with yarn for thy wares: bright iron, cassia, and calamus, were among thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.kjv: Dan also and Javan going to and fro occupied in thy fairs: bright iron, cassia, and calamus, were in thy market.
public_domain_references.brenton: Out of Asel [came] wrought iron, and there is the sound of wheels among thy trading [population].

pob.text: Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding[a].

spob.text: Dedan traded with you, supplying cloths used with riding saddles.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Dedan was your merchant in precious saddle blankets for riding.
public_domain_references.asv: Dedan was thy trafficker in precious cloths for riding.
public_domain_references.kjv: Dedan [was] thy merchant in precious clothes for chariots.
public_domain_references.brenton: [The people of] Dædan were thy merchants, with choice cattle for chariots.

pob.text: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar—they were your traders[a]; in lambs, rams, and male goats[b], in these they traded with you.

spob.text: Arabia[a] and all the princes of Kedar were your trading partners. They traded lambs, rams, and male goats with you.

public_domain_references.bsb: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers, trading in lambs, rams, and goats.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your favorite dealers in lambs, rams, and goats. In these, they were your merchants.
public_domain_references.asv: Arabia, and all the princes of Kedar, they were the merchants of thy hand; in lambs, and rams, and goats, in these were they thy merchants.
public_domain_references.kjv: Arabia, and all the princes of Kedar, they occupied with thee in lambs, and rams, and goats: in these [were they] thy merchants.
public_domain_references.brenton: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar, these were thy traders with thee, [bringing] camels, and lambs, and rams, in which they trade with thee.

pob.text: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah—they were your merchants; with the finest of every spice[a], with every precious stone, and gold, they paid for your wares.

spob.text: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah did business with you. They paid for your goods with the finest of every kind of spice, precious stones of every kind, and gold.

public_domain_references.bsb: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your wares they exchanged gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders. They traded for your wares with the best of all spices, all precious stones, and gold.
public_domain_references.asv: The traffickers of Sheba and Raamah, they were thy traffickers; they traded for thy wares with the chief of all spices, and with all precious stones, and gold.
public_domain_references.kjv: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah, they [were] thy merchants: they occupied in thy fairs with chief of all spices, and with all precious stones, and gold.
public_domain_references.brenton: The merchants of Sabba and Ramma, these were thy merchants, with choice spices, and precious stones: and they brought gold to thy market.

pob.text: Haran and Canneh and Eden[a], the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Kilmad[b], traded with you.

spob.text: Haran, Canneh[a], and Eden traded with you, as did merchants from Sheba, Asshur[b], and Kilmad.

public_domain_references.bsb: Haran, Canneh, and Eden traded with you, and so did the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“Haran, Canneh, Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad, were your traders.
public_domain_references.asv: Haran and Canneh and Eden, the traffickers of Sheba, Asshur [and] Chilmad, were thy traffickers.
public_domain_references.kjv: Haran, and Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, [and] Chilmad, [were] thy merchants.
public_domain_references.brenton: Charra, and Chanaa, these were thy merchants: Assur, and Charman, were thy merchants:

pob.text: They were your merchants in choice wares[a], in wraps of blue and embroidered cloth, and in treasuries of multicolored fabrics, bound with cords and secured[b], among your merchandise.

spob.text: They were your merchants, supplying high-quality goods: rolls of blue cloth, embroidered cloth, and valuable bundles of multicolored fabrics.[a] These goods were tied with cords and secured among your merchandise.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: In your marketplace they traded with you fine garments of blue, embroidered work, and multicolored rugs with cords tightly twisted and knotted.
public_domain_references.web: These were your traders in choice wares, in wrappings of blue and embroidered work, and in cedar chests of rich clothing bound with cords, among your merchandise.
public_domain_references.asv: These were thy traffickers in choice wares, in wrappings of blue and broidered work, and in chests of rich apparel, bound with cords and made of cedar, among thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.kjv: These [were] thy merchants in all sorts [of things], in blue clothes, and broidered work, and in chests of rich apparel, bound with cords, and made of cedar, among thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.brenton: bringing [for] merchandise blue, and choice stores bound with cords, and cypress wood.

pob.text: The ships of Tarshish were your carriers for your merchandise[b][a], and you were filled and became very heavy in the heart of the seas.

spob.text: The ships of Tarshish carried your trade goods. There in the heart of the seas,[a] you were filled with cargo and became very heavy.

public_domain_references.bsb: The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise. And you were filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.
public_domain_references.web: “‘“The ships of Tarshish were your caravans for your merchandise. You were replenished and made very glorious in the heart of the seas.
public_domain_references.asv: The ships of Tarshish were thy caravans for thy merchandise: and thou wast replenished, and made very glorious in the heart of the seas.
public_domain_references.kjv: The ships of Tarshish did sing of thee in thy market: and thou wast replenished, and made very glorious in the midst of the seas.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ships were thy merchants, in abundance, with thy trading [population]: and thou wast filled and very heavily loaded in the heart of the sea.

pob.text: Into great waters your rowers brought you[b][a]; the east wind shattered you in the heart of the seas.

spob.text: Your rowers took you out into the vast waters.[a] Then the east wind shattered you in the midst of the seas.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Your oarsmen have brought you onto the high seas, but the east wind will shatter you in the heart of the sea.
public_domain_references.web: Your rowers have brought you into great waters. The east wind has broken you in the heart of the seas.
public_domain_references.asv: Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the east wind hath broken thee in the heart of the seas.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the east wind hath broken thee in the midst of the seas.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the south wind has broken thee in the heart of the sea.

pob.text: Your wealth[a], your wares, your merchandise, your sailors, and your pilots, those who repair your damage, and those who trade in your merchandise, and all your men of war who are in you, with all your assembly that is in your midst[b], will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.

spob.text: On the day of your downfall, all these will fall into the heart of the seas: your wealth, wares, and merchandise; your sailors and pilots; those who repair your ship;[a] those who trade in your merchandise; all your fighting men; and everyone gathered within you.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Your wealth, wares, and merchandise, your sailors, captains, and shipwrights, your merchants and all the warriors within you, with all the other people on board, will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your downfall.
public_domain_references.web: Your riches, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of war who are in you, with all your company which is among you, will fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin.
public_domain_references.asv: Thy riches, and thy wares, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the dealers in thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that are in thee, with all thy company which is in the midst of thee, shall fall into the heart of the seas in the day of thy ruin.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thy riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that [are] in thee, and in all thy company which [is] in the midst of thee, shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy forces, and thy gain, and that of thy traders, and thy rowers, and thy pilots, and thy counsellors, and they that traffic with thee, and all thy warriors that are in thee: and all thy company in the midst of thee shall perish in the heart of the sea, in the day of thy fall.

pob.text: At the sound of the cry of your pilots[b][a], the pasturelands will quake.

spob.text: When your pilots[a] cry out, the pasturelands[b] will quake.

public_domain_references.bsb: The countryside will shake when your sailors cry out.
public_domain_references.web: At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the pasture lands will shake.
public_domain_references.asv: At the sound of the cry of thy pilots the suburbs shall shake.
public_domain_references.kjv: The suburbs shall shake at the sound of the cry of thy pilots.
public_domain_references.brenton: At the cry of thy voice thy pilots shall be greatly terrified.

pob.text: And all who handle the oar will come down from their ships[a]; the sailors, all the mariners of the sea[b], will stand on the land.

spob.text: All who work the oars will come down from their ships. The sailors—all who sail the sea—will stand on shore.

public_domain_references.bsb: All who handle the oars will abandon their ships. The sailors and all the captains of the sea will stand on the shore.
public_domain_references.web: All who handle the oars, the mariners and all the pilots of the sea, will come down from their ships. They will stand on the land,
public_domain_references.asv: And all that handle the oar, the mariners, [and] all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships; they shall stand upon the land,
public_domain_references.kjv: And all that handle the oar, the mariners, [and] all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships, they shall stand upon the land;
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the rowers and the mariners shall come down from the ships, and the pilots of the sea shall stand on the land.

pob.text: They will make their voice heard over you and cry out bitterly[a]; they will throw dust on their heads[b]; they will roll in ashes.

spob.text: They will raise their voices in mourning for you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.

public_domain_references.bsb: They will raise their voices for you and cry out bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
public_domain_references.web: and will cause their voice to be heard over you, and will cry bitterly. They will cast up dust on their heads. They will wallow in the ashes.
public_domain_references.asv: and shall cause their voice to be heard over thee, and shall cry bitterly, and shall cast up dust upon their heads; they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:
public_domain_references.kjv: And shall cause their voice to be heard against thee, and shall cry bitterly, and shall cast up dust upon their heads, they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:
public_domain_references.brenton: And they shall wail over thee with their voice, and cry bitterly, and put earth on their heads, and spread ashes under them.

pob.text: They will make themselves bald for you[a], and put on sackcloth, and they will weep over you with bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.

spob.text: They will shave their heads bald for you and put on sackcloth. They will weep over you in deep inner anguish and bitter mourning.

public_domain_references.bsb: They will shave their heads for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth. They will weep over you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning.
public_domain_references.web: They will make themselves bald for you, and clothe themselves with sackcloth. They will weep for you in bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.
public_domain_references.asv: and they shall make themselves bald for thee, and gird them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for thee in bitterness of soul with bitter mourning.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they shall make themselves utterly bald for thee, and gird them with sackcloth, and they shall weep for thee with bitterness of heart [and] bitter wailing.

pob.text: They will raise a lamentation over you in their wailing[a], and they will lament over you: ‘Who is like Tyre[b], silenced in the midst of the sea?’

spob.text: As they wail,[a] they will make a funeral lament for you. They will mourn over you and say, “Who is like Tyre, silenced in the middle of the sea?”[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: As they wail and mourn over you, they will take up a lament for you: ‘Who was ever like Tyre, silenced in the middle of the sea?
public_domain_references.web: In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you, and lament over you, saying, ‘Who is there like Tyre, like her who is brought to silence in the middle of the sea?’
public_domain_references.asv: And in their wailing they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and lament over thee, [saying], Who is there like Tyre, like her that is brought to silence in the midst of the sea?
public_domain_references.kjv: And in their wailing they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and lament over thee, [saying], What [city is] like Tyrus, like the destroyed in the midst of the sea?
public_domain_references.brenton: And their sons shall take up a [lament] for thee, even a lamentation for Sor, [saying],

pob.text: When your wares went out from the seas[a], you satisfied many peoples[b]; with your abundant wealth and your merchandise you enriched the kings of the earth.

spob.text: When your cargo went out from the seas, you supplied many peoples abundantly. Your great wealth and merchandise made the kings of the earth rich.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: When your wares went out to sea, you satisfied many nations. You enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant wealth and merchandise.
public_domain_references.web: When your wares came from the seas, you filled many peoples. You enriched the kings of the earth with the multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.
public_domain_references.asv: When thy wares went forth out of the seas, thou filledst many peoples; thou didst enrich the kings of the earth with the multitude of thy riches and of thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.kjv: When thy wares went forth out of the seas, thou filledst many people; thou didst enrich the kings of the earth with the multitude of thy riches and of thy merchandise.
public_domain_references.brenton: How large a reward hast thou gained from the sea? thou hast filled nations out of thine abundance; and out of thy mixed merchandise thou hast enriched all the kings of the earth.

pob.text: At the time you were broken by the seas in the depths of the waters[b][a], your merchandise and all your assembly in your midst fell.

spob.text: When the seas broke you apart in the deep waters, your merchandise and all those gathered within you fell.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and the people among you have gone down with you.
public_domain_references.web: In the time that you were broken by the seas, in the depths of the waters, your merchandise and all your company fell within you.
public_domain_references.asv: In the time that thou wast broken by the seas in the depths of the waters, thy merchandise and all thy company did fall in the midst of thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the time [when] thou shalt be broken by the seas in the depths of the waters thy merchandise and all thy company in the midst of thee shall fall.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now art thou broken in the sea, thy traders are in the deep water, and all thy company in the midst of thee: all thy rowers have fallen.

pob.text: All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled at you[a], and their kings shudder with horror[c][b]; their faces are convulsed.

spob.text: All who live in the coastal lands[a] are appalled at you. Their kings shudder with horror, and their faces contort.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: All the people of the coastlands are appalled over you. Their kings shudder with fear; their faces are contorted.
public_domain_references.web: All the inhabitants of the islands are astonished at you, and their kings are horribly afraid. They are troubled in their face.
public_domain_references.asv: All the inhabitants of the isles are astonished at thee, and their kings are horribly afraid; they are troubled in their countenance.
public_domain_references.kjv: All the inhabitants of the isles shall be astonished at thee, and their kings shall be sore afraid, they shall be troubled in [their] countenance.
public_domain_references.brenton: All the dwellers in the islands have mourned over thee, and their kings have been utterly amazed, and their countenance has wept.

pob.text: Merchants among the peoples hiss at you[a]; you have become a horror[b], and you will be no more forever.

spob.text: Merchants who trade among different peoples hiss at you.[a] You have become something horrifying, and you will be gone forever.

public_domain_references.bsb: Those who trade among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more.’”
public_domain_references.web: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you. You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.”’”
public_domain_references.asv: The merchants among the peoples hiss at thee; thou art become a terror, and thou shalt nevermore have any being.
public_domain_references.kjv: The merchants among the people shall hiss at thee; thou shalt be a terror, and never [shalt be] any more.
public_domain_references.brenton: Merchants from the nations have hissed at thee; thou art utterly destroyed, and shalt not be any more for ever.

pob.text: And the word of Yahweh came to me[a], saying,

spob.text: Then Yahweh[a] gave me this message:

public_domain_references.bsb: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh’s word came again to me, saying,
public_domain_references.asv: The word of Jehovah came again unto me, saying,
public_domain_references.kjv: The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying,
public_domain_references.brenton: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

pob.text: Son of man[a], say to the prince of Tyre, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: Because your heart is proud, and you say, “I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the seas,” yet you are a man and not a god[b], though you set your heart like the heart of gods.”

spob.text: Son of man, tell the prince of Tyre, “This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have become proud, you say, ‘I am a god. I sit in the seat of gods, in the heart of the seas.’[a] But you are a man, not a god, though you think you are like the gods.[b]”

public_domain_references.bsb: “Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre that this is what the Lord GOD says: Your heart is proud, and you have said, ‘I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the sea.’ Yet you are a man and not a god, though you have regarded your heart as that of a god.
public_domain_references.web: “Son of man, tell the prince of Tyre, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: “Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, ‘I am a god, I sit in the seat of God, in the middle of the seas;’ yet you are man, and no god, though you set your heart as the heart of a god—
public_domain_references.asv: Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyre, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Because thy heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a god, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art man, and not God, though thou didst set thy heart as the heart of God;—
public_domain_references.kjv: Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thine heart [is] lifted up, and thou hast said, I [am] a God, I sit [in] the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou [art] a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:

spob.text: I will scatter the people of Egypt among the nations and spread them throughout many lands. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
public_domain_references.web: I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’”
public_domain_references.asv: And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them through the countries; and they shall know that I am Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them among the countries; and they shall know that I [am] the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations, and utterly scatter them among the countries; and they all shall know that I am the Lord.

pob.text: And it happened in the eleventh year[a], in the third month, on the first day of the month, that the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,

spob.text: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, this message from Yahweh[a] came to me:
