public_domain_references.kjv: And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third [month], in the first [day] of the month, [that] the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first [day] of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

pob.text: Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?

spob.text: “Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and the multitude with him: ‘In your greatness, whom are you like?’”

public_domain_references.bsb: “Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: ‘Who can be compared to your greatness?
public_domain_references.web: “Son of man, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude: ‘Whom are you like in your greatness?
public_domain_references.asv: Son of man, say unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude: Whom art thou like in thy greatness?
public_domain_references.kjv: Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness?
public_domain_references.brenton: Son of man, say to Pharao king of Egypt, and to his multitude; To whom hast thou compared thyself in thy haughtiness?

pob.text: Behold[a], Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in branches and a forest giving shade, and lofty in height[b]; its top was among the clouds.

spob.text: Look! Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon.[a] It had beautiful branches and was like a forest that gave shade. It towered high, and its top was among the clouds.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Look at Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches that shaded the forest. It towered on high; its top was among the clouds.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with beautiful branches, and with a forest-like shade, of high stature; and its top was among the thick boughs.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a forest-like shade, and of high stature; and its top was among the thick boughs.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Behold, the Assyrian [was] a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold, the Assyrian was a cypress in Libanus, and was fair in shoots, and high in stature: his top reached to the midst of the clouds.

pob.text: Waters made it grow[a]; the deep made it rise high. Its rivers flowed all around its planting place[b], and it sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.

spob.text: The waters made the tree grow, and the deep made it tower high. Rivers from the deep flowed all around the ground where it was planted, and the deep sent out channels of water to all the trees of the field.

public_domain_references.bsb: The waters made it grow; the deep springs made it tall, directing their streams all around its base and sending their channels to all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.web: The waters nourished it. The deep made it to grow. Its rivers ran all around its plantation. It sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.asv: The waters nourished it, the deep made it to grow: the rivers thereof ran round about its plantation; and it sent out its channels unto all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.kjv: The waters made him great, the deep set him up on high with her rivers running round about his plants, and sent out her little rivers unto all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.brenton: The water nourished him, the depth made him grow tall; she led her rivers round about his plants, and she sent forth her streams to all the trees of the field.

pob.text: Therefore its height rose above all the trees of the field[a], and its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long because of abundant waters as it spread out.

spob.text: Therefore it grew taller than all the trees of the field. Its large limbs increased in number, and its branches grew long because of abundant waters as it spread outward.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore it towered higher than all the trees of the field. Its branches multiplied, and its boughs grew long as it spread them out because of the abundant waters.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore its stature was exalted above all the trees of the field; and its boughs were multiplied. Its branches became long by reason of many waters, when it spread them out.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore its stature was exalted above all the trees of the field; and its boughs were multiplied, and its branches became long by reason of many waters, when it shot [them] forth.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore his height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and his boughs were multiplied, and his branches became long because of the multitude of waters, when he shot forth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore was his stature exalted above all the trees of the field, and his branches spread far by the help of much water.

pob.text: In its branches all the birds of the heavens nested[a], and under its boughs all the beasts of the field gave birth, and in its shade all the many nations dwelt.

spob.text: All the birds of the sky made their nests in its branches. All the wild animals gave birth beneath its leafy branches. All the many nations lived in its shade.

public_domain_references.bsb: All the birds of the air nested in its branches, and all the beasts of the field gave birth beneath its boughs; all the great nations lived in its shade.
public_domain_references.web: All the birds of the sky made their nests in its boughs. Under its branches, all the animals of the field gave birth to their young. All great nations lived under its shadow.
public_domain_references.asv: All the birds of the heavens made their nests in its boughs; and under its branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young; and under its shadow dwelt all great nations.
public_domain_references.kjv: All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young, and under his shadow dwelt all great nations.
public_domain_references.brenton: All the birds of the sky made their nests in his boughs, and under his branches all the wild beasts of the field bred; the whole multitude of nations dwelt under his shadow.

pob.text: So it was beautiful in its greatness[a], in the length of its branches, because its root was by abundant waters.

spob.text: The tree was beautiful, great in size and with long branches, because its root was beside abundant water.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its limbs, for its roots extended to abundant waters.
public_domain_references.web: Thus it was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches; for its root was by many waters.
public_domain_references.asv: Thus was it fair in its greatness, in the length of its branches; for its root was by many waters.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches: for his root was by great waters.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he was fair in his height by reason of the multitude of his branches: for his roots were amidst much water.

pob.text: Cedars did not overshadow it in the garden of God[a]; cypresses did not compare with its boughs, and plane trees were not like its branches[b]. No tree in the garden of God compared with it in its beauty.

spob.text: The cedars did not overshadow it in the garden of God.[a] The cypresses did not match its main branches, and the plane trees had no branches like its own.[b] No tree in the garden of God could match its beauty.

public_domain_references.bsb: The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it; the cypresses could not compare with its branches, nor the plane trees match its boughs. No tree in the garden of God could compare with its beauty.
public_domain_references.web: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it. The cypress trees were not like its branches. The pine trees were not like its branches; nor was any tree in the garden of God like it in its beauty.
public_domain_references.asv: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it; the fir-trees were not like its boughs, and the plane-trees were not as its branches; nor was any tree in the garden of God like unto it in its beauty.
public_domain_references.kjv: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.
public_domain_references.brenton: And such cypresses [as this] were in the paradise of God; and there were no pines like his shoots, and there were no firs like his branches: no tree in the paradise of God was like him in his beauty,

pob.text: I made it beautiful with its many branches[a], and all the trees of Eden that were in the garden of God envied it.

spob.text: I made it beautiful with so many branches,[a] and all the trees of Eden in the garden of God envied it.

public_domain_references.bsb: I made it beautiful with its many branches, the envy of all the trees of Eden, which were in the garden of God.’
public_domain_references.web: I made it beautiful by the multitude of its branches, so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied it.’
public_domain_references.asv: I made it fair by the multitude of its branches, so that all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied it.
public_domain_references.kjv: I have made him fair by the multitude of his branches: so that all the trees of Eden, that [were] in the garden of God, envied him.
public_domain_references.brenton: because of the multitude of his branches: and the trees of God's paradise of delight envied him.

pob.text: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you grew tall in stature[a], and set your top among the thick boughs, and his heart was lifted up in his height,

spob.text: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you grew very tall, and he lifted his treetop among the thick boughs,[a] and his heart became proud because of his height—[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Since it became great in height and set its top among the clouds, and it grew proud on account of its height,
public_domain_references.web: “Therefore thus said the Lord Yahweh: ‘Because he is exalted in stature, and he has set his top among the thick branches, and his heart is lifted up in his height,
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore thus said the Lord Jehovah: Because thou art exalted in stature, and he hath set his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height, and he hath shot up his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height;
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore thus saith the Lord; Because thou art grown great, and hast set thy top in the midst of the clouds, and I saw when he was exalted;

pob.text: I gave him into the hand of a mighty one of the nations; he will surely deal with him[a]. According to his wickedness I drove him out.

spob.text: I handed him over to a powerful ruler from among the nations. He will certainly act against him. I drove him out as his wickedness deserved.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I delivered it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal with it according to its wickedness. I have banished it.
public_domain_references.web: I will deliver him into the hand of the mighty one of the nations. He will surely deal with him. I have driven him out for his wickedness.
public_domain_references.asv: I will even deliver him into the hand of the mighty one of the nations; he shall surely deal with him; I have driven him out for his wickedness.
public_domain_references.kjv: I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him: I have driven him out for his wickedness.
public_domain_references.brenton: therefore I delivered him into the hands of the prince of the nations, and he wrought his destruction.

pob.text: Foreigners[a], the ruthless of the nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley, and its boughs were broken in all the channels of the land[c][b]. Then all the peoples of the earth went down from its shade and left it.

spob.text: Ruthless foreigners from among the nations cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley. Its large branches were broken in all the streambeds of the land. Then all the peoples of the earth went down from its shade and left it behind.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches have fallen on the mountains and in every valley; its boughs lay broken in all the earth’s ravines. And all the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it.
public_domain_references.web: Foreigners, the tyrants of the nations, have cut him off and have left him. His branches have fallen on the mountains and in all the valleys, and his boughs are broken by all the watercourses of the land. All the peoples of the earth have gone down from his shadow and have left him.
public_domain_references.asv: And strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off, and have left him: upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken by all the watercourses of the land; and all the peoples of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off, and have left him: upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken by all the rivers of the land; and all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And ravaging strangers from the nations have destroyed him, and have cast him down upon the mountains: his branches fell in all the valleys, and his boughs were broken in every field of the land; and all the people of the nations are gone down from their shelter, and have laid him low.

pob.text: On its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens will dwell[b][a], and on its boughs will be all the beasts of the field.

spob.text: All the birds of the sky will live on its fallen trunk,[a] and all the animals of the field will be on its branches.

public_domain_references.bsb: All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field lived among its boughs.
public_domain_references.web: All the birds of the sky will dwell on his ruin, and all the animals of the field will be on his branches,
public_domain_references.asv: Upon his ruin all the birds of the heavens shall dwell, and all the beasts of the field shall be upon his branches;
public_domain_references.kjv: Upon his ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain, and all the beasts of the field shall be upon his branches:
public_domain_references.brenton: All the birds of the sky have settled on his fallen trunk, and all the wild beasts of the field came upon his boughs:

pob.text: so that all the trees by the waters may not grow tall in their height[a], and may not set their treetop among the clouds, and that none of the water-drinkers may stand over them in their height; for all of them are given over to death, to the land below, among the sons of man[b], with those who go down to the pit.

spob.text: God did this so that no tree by the waters would rise so high or lift its treetop among the clouds.[a] No tree that drinks water would tower over the others.[b] For all of them are given over to death—to the land below, among the sons of man,[c] with those who go down to the pit.

public_domain_references.bsb: This happened so that no other trees by the waters would become great in height and set their tops among the clouds, and no other well-watered trees would reach them in height. For they have all been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the mortals who descend to the Pit.’
public_domain_references.web: to the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves in their stature, and don’t set their top among the thick boughs. Their mighty ones don’t stand up on their height, even all who drink water; for they are all delivered to death, to the lower parts of the earth, among the children of men, with those who go down to the pit.’
public_domain_references.asv: to the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves in their stature, neither set their top among the thick boughs, nor that their mighty ones stand up in their height, [even] all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.
public_domain_references.kjv: To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their trees stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.
public_domain_references.brenton: in order that none of the trees by the water should exalt themselves by reason of their size: whereas they set their top in the midst of the clouds, yet they continued not in their high state in their place, all that drank water, all were consigned to death, to the depth of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.

pob.text: Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day he went down to Sheol[a], I caused mourning; I covered the deep because of him, and I restrained its rivers, and the many waters were stopped. I made Lebanon grow dark because of him[c][b], and all the trees of the field fainted because of him.

spob.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: When he went down to Sheol,[a] I brought mourning. Because of him, I covered the deep, held back its rivers, and stopped its abundant waters. I brought darkness over Lebanon because of him, and all the trees of the field fainted because of him.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘On the day it was brought down to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the deep because of it; I held back its rivers; its abundant waters were restrained. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.
public_domain_references.web: “The Lord Yahweh says: ‘In the day when he went down to Sheol, I caused a mourning. I covered the deep for him, and I restrained its rivers. The great waters were stopped. I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.
public_domain_references.asv: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In the day when he went down to Sheol I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the rivers thereof; and the great waters were stayed; and I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed: and I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus saith the Lord God; In the day wherein he went down to Hades, the deep mourned for him: and I stayed her floods, and restrained her abundance of water: and Libanus saddened for him, all the trees of the field fainted for him.

pob.text: At the sound of his fall I made nations quake[a], when I brought him down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit; and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water[c][b], were comforted in the earth beneath.

spob.text: At the sound of his fall, I made the nations quake when I brought him down to Sheol[a] with those who descend into the pit. In the earth beneath, all the trees of Eden were comforted[b]—the finest and best of Lebanon, all the trees that drink water.

public_domain_references.bsb: I made the nations quake at the sound of its downfall, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the Pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees, were consoled in the earth below.
public_domain_references.web: I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to Sheol with those who descend into the pit. All the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the lower parts of the earth.
public_domain_references.asv: I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to Sheol with them that descend into the pit; and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the nether parts of the earth.
public_domain_references.kjv: I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell with them that descend into the pit: and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.
public_domain_references.brenton: At the sound of his fall the nations quaked, when I brought him down to Hades with them that go down to the pit: and all the trees of Delight comforted him in the heart, and the choice [plants] of Libanus, all that drink water.

pob.text: They too went down with it to Sheol[a], to those slain by the sword; its arm dwelt in its shade among the nations.

spob.text: They too went down with it to Sheol,[a] joining those killed by the sword. Those who had been its arm had lived in its shade among the nations.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: They too descended with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword. As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations.
public_domain_references.web: They also went down into Sheol with him to those who are slain by the sword; yes, those who were his arm, who lived under his shadow in the middle of the nations.
public_domain_references.asv: They also went down into Sheol with him unto them that are slain by the sword; yea, they that were his arm, [that] dwelt under his shadow in the midst of the nations.
public_domain_references.kjv: They also went down into hell with him unto [them that be] slain with the sword; and [they that were] his arm, [that] dwelt under his shadow in the midst of the heathen.
public_domain_references.brenton: For they went down to hell with him among the slain with the sword; and his seed, [even] they that dwelt under his shadow, perished in the midst of their life.

pob.text: Whom were you like in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the land below; you shall lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude[a], declares the Lord GOD.

spob.text: Who among the trees of Eden was like you in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down with Eden’s trees to the land of the dead below.[a] You will lie among the uncircumcised,[b] with those killed by the sword. This is what will happen to Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You also will be brought down to the depths of the earth to be with the trees of Eden. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.’”
public_domain_references.web: “‘To whom are you thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lower parts of the earth. You will lie in the middle of the uncircumcised, with those who are slain by the sword. “‘This is Pharaoh and all his multitude,’ says the Lord Yahweh.”
public_domain_references.asv: To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth: thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised, with them that are slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth: thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with [them that be] slain by the sword. This [is] Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.brenton: To whom art thou compared? descend, and be thou debased with the trees of paradise to the depth of the earth: thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that are slain by the sword. Thus shall Pharao be, and the multitude of his host, saith the Lord God.

pob.text: And it happened in the twelfth year[a], in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, that the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,

spob.text: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, Yahweh spoke to me:

public_domain_references.bsb: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
public_domain_references.web: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first day of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first [day] of the month, that the word of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
public_domain_references.kjv: And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first [day] of the month, [that] the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the tenth month, on the first [day] of the month, [that] the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

pob.text: Son of man[a], raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: You compared yourself to a young lion among the nations, but you were like the monster in the seas; you burst forth in your rivers, and muddied the waters with your feet[c][b], and fouled their rivers.

spob.text:
Son of man, sing a funeral song over Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Say to him:

“You compared yourself to a young lion among the nations,[a]
but you were like a great monster in the seas.[b]
You surged through your rivers,
stirred up the waters with your feet and made them muddy,
and fouled their rivers.”[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Son of man, take up a lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: ‘You are like a lion among the nations; you are like a monster in the seas. You thrash about in your rivers, churning up the waters with your feet and muddying the streams.’
public_domain_references.web: “Son of man, take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and tell him, ‘You were likened to a young lion of the nations; yet you are as a monster in the seas. You broke out with your rivers, and troubled the waters with your feet, and fouled their rivers.’”
public_domain_references.asv: Son of man, take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say unto him, Thou wast likened unto a young lion of the nations: yet art thou as a monster in the seas; and thou didst break forth with thy rivers, and troubledst the waters with thy feet, and fouledst their rivers.
public_domain_references.kjv: Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say unto him, Thou art like a young lion of the nations, and thou [art] as a whale in the seas: and thou camest forth with thy rivers, and troubledst the waters with thy feet, and fouledst their rivers.
public_domain_references.brenton: Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharao king of Egypt, and say to him, Thou art become like a lion of the nations, and as the serpent that is in the sea: and thou didst make assaults with thy rivers, and didst disturb the water with thy feet, and didst trample thy rivers.

pob.text: Thus says the Lord GOD: I will spread my net over you with an assembly of many peoples[b][a], and they will haul you up in my dragnet.

spob.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “I will spread my net over you with a large gathering of peoples, and they will haul you up in my dragnet.”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will spread My net over you with a company of many peoples, and they will draw you up in My net.
public_domain_references.web: The Lord Yahweh says: “I will spread out my net on you with a company of many peoples. They will bring you up in my net.
public_domain_references.asv: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: I will spread out my net upon thee with a company of many peoples; and they shall bring thee up in my net.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will therefore spread out my net over thee with a company of many people; and they shall bring thee up in my net.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus saith the Lord; I will also cast over thee the nets of many nations, and will bring thee up with my hook:

pob.text: I will cast you onto the land[a]; I will throw you down on the open field, and I will cause every bird of the heavens to settle on you[b], and I will satisfy the beasts of all the earth with you.

spob.text: I will cast you onto the land and throw you down in the open field. I will make every bird of the sky settle on you, and wild animals from all over the earth will eat you until they are full.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field. I will cause all the birds of the air to settle upon you, and all the beasts of the earth to eat their fill of you.
public_domain_references.web: I will leave you on the land. I will cast you out on the open field, and will cause all the birds of the sky to settle on you. I will satisfy the animals of the whole earth with you.
public_domain_references.asv: And I will leave thee upon the land, I will cast thee forth upon the open field, and will cause all the birds of the heavens to settle upon thee, and I will satisfy the beasts of the whole earth with thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then will I leave thee upon the land, I will cast thee forth upon the open field, and will cause all the fowls of the heaven to remain upon thee, and I will fill the beasts of the whole earth with thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: and I will stretch thee upon the earth: the fields shall be covered [with thee], and I will cause all the birds of the sky to settle upon thee, and I will fill [with thee] all the wild beasts of the earth.

pob.text: And I will put your flesh on the mountains[a], and I will fill the valleys with your carcass.

spob.text: I will lay your flesh on the mountains. I will fill the valleys with your carcass.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
public_domain_references.web: I will lay your flesh on the mountains, and fill the valleys with your height.
public_domain_references.asv: And I will lay thy flesh upon the mountains, and fill the valleys with thy height.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I will lay thy flesh upon the mountains, and fill the valleys with thy height.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will cast thy flesh upon the mountains, and will saturate [them] with thy blood.

pob.text: I will drench the land with your flowing blood up to the mountains[c][b][a], and the ravines will be filled with you.

spob.text: I will soak the land with your flowing blood, all the way to the mountains. The ravines will be filled with you.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I will drench the land with the flow of your blood, all the way to the mountains— the ravines will be filled.
public_domain_references.web: I will also water the land in which you swim with your blood, even to the mountains. The watercourses will be full of you.
public_domain_references.asv: I will also water with thy blood the land wherein thou swimmest, even to the mountains; and the watercourses shall be full of thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will also water with thy blood the land wherein thou swimmest, [even] to the mountains; and the rivers shall be full of thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the land shall be drenched with thy dung, because of thy multitude upon the mountains: I will fill the valleys with thee.

pob.text: When I extinguish you[a], I will cover the heavens and darken their stars; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.

spob.text: When I extinguish you[a], I will cover the heavens and make their stars go dark. I will hide the sun behind a cloud, and the moon will give no light.

public_domain_references.bsb: When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
public_domain_references.web: When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and make its stars dark. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon won’t give its light.
public_domain_references.asv: And when I shall extinguish thee, I will cover the heavens, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give its light.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will veil the heavens when thou art extinguished, and will darken the stars thereof; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.

pob.text: All the lights of light in the heavens I will darken over you[a], and I will put darkness over your land, declares the Lord GOD.

spob.text: I will make all the shining lights in the heavens dark over you. I will bring darkness over your land, declares the Lord Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: All the shining lights in the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land,’ declares the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.web: I will make all the bright lights of the sky dark over you, and set darkness on your land,” says the Lord Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land, saith the Lord Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land, saith the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.brenton: All the [bodies] that give light in the sky, shall be darkened over thee, and I will bring darkness upon the earth, saith the Lord God.

pob.text: And I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring your ruin among the nations[c][b][a], into lands that you have not known.

spob.text: I will throw the hearts of many peoples into turmoil[a] when I bring your ruin among the nations, into foreign lands you have never known.

public_domain_references.bsb: ‘I will trouble the hearts of many peoples, when I bring about your destruction among the nations, in countries you do not know.
public_domain_references.web: “I will also trouble the hearts of many peoples, when I bring your destruction among the nations, into the countries which you have not known.
public_domain_references.asv: I will also vex the hearts of many peoples, when I shall bring thy destruction among the nations, into the countries which thou hast not known.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will also vex the hearts of many people, when I shall bring thy destruction among the nations, into the countries which thou hast not known.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will provoke to anger the heart of many people, when I shall lead thee captive among the nations, to a land which thou hast not known.

pob.text: I will make many peoples appalled at you[a], and their kings will shudder over you when I brandish my sword before them; and they will tremble every moment, each man for his own life[c][b], on the day of your downfall.

spob.text: I will fill many peoples with horror because of what happens to you. Their kings will shudder at what happens to you when I swing my sword before them. On the day you fall, they will tremble from moment to moment, each man fearing for his own life.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will cause many peoples to be appalled over you, and their kings will shudder in horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them. On the day of your downfall each of them will tremble every moment for his life.’
public_domain_references.web: Yes, I will make many peoples amazed at you, and their kings will be horribly afraid for you, when I brandish my sword before them. They will tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of your fall.”
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, I will make many peoples amazed at thee, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them; and they shall tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yea, I will make many people amazed at thee, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them; and they shall tremble at [every] moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall.
public_domain_references.brenton: And many nations shall mourn over thee, and their kings shall be utterly amazed, when my sword flies in their faces, as they wait for their [own] fall from the day of thy fall.

pob.text: For thus says the Lord GOD: The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you[a].

spob.text: For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: The king of Babylon’s sword will come to attack you.

public_domain_references.bsb: For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you!
public_domain_references.web: For the Lord Yahweh says: “The sword of the king of Babylon will come on you.
public_domain_references.asv: For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ For thus saith the Lord GOD; The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: For thus saith the Lord God; The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee,

pob.text: By the swords of mighty men I will make your multitude fall— all of them the ruthless ones of the nations[a]. They will plunder the pride of Egypt[b], and all her multitude will be destroyed.

spob.text: I will use the swords of mighty warriors to bring down your great multitude. These warriors are all ruthless men from the nations. They will plunder Egypt’s pride,[a] and all her multitude will be destroyed.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will make your hordes fall by the swords of the mighty, the most ruthless of all nations. They will ravage the pride of Egypt and all her multitudes will be destroyed.
public_domain_references.web: I will cause your multitude to fall by the swords of the mighty. They are all the ruthless of the nations. They will bring the pride of Egypt to nothing, and all its multitude will be destroyed.
public_domain_references.asv: By the swords of the mighty will I cause thy multitude to fall; the terrible of the nations are they all: and they shall bring to nought the pride of Egypt, and all the multitude thereof shall be destroyed.
public_domain_references.kjv: By the swords of the mighty will I cause thy multitude to fall, the terrible of the nations, all of them: and they shall spoil the pomp of Egypt, and all the multitude thereof shall be destroyed.
public_domain_references.brenton: with the swords of mighty men; and I will cast down thy strength: [they are] all destroying ones from the nations, and they shall destroy the pride of Egypt, and all her strength shall be crushed.

pob.text: And I will destroy all its beasts from beside its abundant waters[a], and no human foot will muddy them anymore[b], nor will the hooves of beasts muddy them.

spob.text: I will destroy all its animals beside its abundant waters. No one will muddy those waters with their feet anymore, and no animals will muddy them with their hooves.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will slaughter all her cattle beside the abundant waters. No human foot will muddy them again, and no cattle hooves will disturb them.
public_domain_references.web: I will destroy also all its animals from beside many waters. The foot of man won’t trouble them any more, nor will the hoofs of animals trouble them.
public_domain_references.asv: I will destroy also all the beasts thereof from beside many waters; neither shall the foot of man trouble them any more, nor the hoofs of beasts trouble them.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will destroy also all the beasts thereof from beside the great waters; neither shall the foot of man trouble them any more, nor the hoofs of beasts trouble them.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will destroy all her cattle from [beside] the great water; and the foot of man shall not trouble it any more, and the step of cattle shall no more trample it.

pob.text: Then I will let their waters settle[a], and I will make their rivers flow like oil[b], declares the Lord GOD.

spob.text: Then I will make their waters still,[a] and I will make their rivers flow smoothly like oil, declares the Lord Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I will let her waters settle and will make her rivers flow like oil,’ declares the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.web: Then I will make their waters clear, and cause their rivers to run like oil,” says the Lord Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: Then will I make their waters clear, and cause their rivers to run like oil, saith the Lord Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then will I make their waters deep, and cause their rivers to run like oil, saith the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus shall their waters then be at rest, and their rivers shall flow like oil, saith the Lord,

pob.text: When I make the land of Egypt a desolation[a], and the land is stripped of all that fills it, when I strike down all who dwell in it, then they will know that I am Yahweh.

spob.text: When I devastate the land of Egypt and strip it of everything that fills it, when I strike down everyone who lives there, then they will know that I am Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: ‘When I make the land of Egypt a desolation and empty it of all that filled it, when I strike down all who live there, then they will know that I am the LORD.’
public_domain_references.web: “When I make the land of Egypt desolate and waste, a land destitute of that of which it was full, when I strike all those who dwell therein, then they will know that I am Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: When I shall make the land of Egypt desolate and waste, a land destitute of that whereof it was full, when I shall smite all them that dwell therein, then shall they know that I am Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: When I shall make the land of Egypt desolate, and the country shall be destitute of that whereof it was full, when I shall smite all them that dwell therein, then shall they know that I [am] the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: when I shall give up Egypt to destruction, and the land shall be made desolate with the fulness thereof; when I shall scatter all that dwell in it, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

pob.text: This is a lamentation[a], and the daughters of the nations will lament over her. They will lament over Egypt and over all her multitude[b], declares the Lord GOD.

spob.text: This is a funeral song. Women from the nations[a] will sing it over Egypt and all its multitude,[b] declares the Lord Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the lament they will chant for her; the daughters of the nations will chant it. Over Egypt and all her multitudes they will chant it, declares the Lord GOD.”
public_domain_references.web: “‘“This is the lamentation with which they will lament. The daughters of the nations will lament with this. They will lament with it over Egypt, and over all her multitude,” says the Lord Yahweh.’”
public_domain_references.asv: This is the lamentation wherewith they shall lament; the daughters of the nations shall lament therewith; over Egypt, and over all her multitude, shall they lament therewith, saith the Lord Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: This [is] the lamentation wherewith they shall lament her: the daughters of the nations shall lament her: they shall lament for her, [even] for Egypt, and for all her multitude, saith the Lord GOD.
public_domain_references.brenton: There is a lamentation, and thou shalt utter it; and the daughters of the nations shall utter it, [even] for Egypt, and they shall mourn for it over all the strength thereof, saith the Lord God.

pob.text: And it happened in the twelfth year[a], on the fifteenth day of the month, that the word of Yahweh came to me, saying,

pob.text: Son of man[a], wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring her down, her and the daughters of mighty nations, to the land beneath[c][b], with those who go down to the pit.

spob.text: Son of man, wail over Egypt’s great multitude. Bring Egypt and the peoples of mighty nations down to the land beneath, among those who descend to the pit.[a][b]

public_domain_references.web: Whom do you pass in beauty? Go down, and be laid with the uncircumcised.
public_domain_references.asv: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.
public_domain_references.kjv: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.

spob.text: They will fall among those killed by the sword.[a] The sword is given. Drag Egypt away, and all her people with her.

pob.text: And I will bring them out from the peoples[a], and gather them from the lands, and bring them into their own land; and I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

public_domain_references.web: The man said to me, “Son of man, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart on all that I will show you; for you have been brought here so that I may show them to you. Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.”
public_domain_references.asv: And the man said unto me, Son of man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears, and set thy heart upon all that I shall show thee; for, to the intent that I may show them unto thee, art thou brought hither: declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the man said unto me, Son of man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears, and set thine heart upon all that I shall shew thee; for to the intent that I might shew [them] unto thee [art] thou brought hither: declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the man said to me, Look with thine eyes at him whom thou hast seen, son of man, and hear with thine ears, and lay up in thine heart all things that I show thee; for thou hast come in hither that [I] might show thee, and thou shalt show all things that thou seest to the house of Israel.

pob.text: And behold[a], there was a wall outside the house, all around, and in the hand of the man was a measuring reed of six cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. And he measured the width of the structure: one reed[b], and the height: one reed.

spob.text: Then I saw a wall outside the house, surrounding the house on every side. The man held a measuring reed six long cubits in length. Each long cubit was one standard cubit plus a handbreadth. He measured the structure: it was one reed wide and one reed high.

public_domain_references.bsb: And I saw a wall surrounding the temple area. Now the length of the measuring rod in the man’s hand was six long cubits (each measuring a cubit and a handbreadth), and he measured the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, there was a wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a hand width each. So he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
public_domain_references.asv: And, behold, a wall on the outside of the house round about, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a handbreadth each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
public_domain_references.kjv: And behold a wall on the outside of the house round about, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed of six cubits [long] by the cubit and an hand breadth: so he measured the breadth of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
public_domain_references.brenton: And behold a wall round about the house without, and in the man's hand a reed, the measure [of it was] six cubits by the cubit, and a span: and he measured across the front wall; the breadth was equal to the reed, and the length of it equal to the reed.

pob.text: Then he came to the gate that faced east[a], and he went up its steps and measured the threshold of the gate: one reed wide. And the other threshold was one reed wide.

spob.text: Then he came to the gate that faced east. He climbed its steps and measured the gate’s threshold. It was one measuring reed wide. The threshold on the other side[a] was also one measuring reed wide.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then he came to the gate facing east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep.
public_domain_references.web: Then he came to the gate which looks toward the east, and went up its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate, one reed wide; and the other threshold, one reed wide.
public_domain_references.asv: Then came he unto the gate which looketh toward the east, and went up the steps thereof: and he measured the threshold of the gate, one reed broad; and the other threshold, one reed broad.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then came he unto the gate which looketh toward the east, and went up the stairs thereof, and measured the threshold of the gate, [which was] one reed broad; and the other threshold [of the gate, which was] one reed broad.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he entered by seven steps into the gate that looks eastward, and he measured across the porch of the gate equal to the reed.

pob.text: And each guardroom was one reed long and one reed wide[a], and between the guardrooms was five cubits[c][b]. And the threshold of the gate beside the portico of the gate on the inside was one reed.

spob.text: Each guardroom was one measuring reed long and one measuring reed wide.[a] The space between the guardrooms was five cubits.[b] On the inner side of the gate, the threshold beside the entrance porch measured one reed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and there were five cubits between the gate chambers. The inner threshold of the gate by the portico facing inward was one rod deep.
public_domain_references.web: Every lodge was one reed long and one reed wide. Between the lodges was five cubits. The threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate toward the house was one reed.
public_domain_references.asv: And every lodge was one reed long, and one reed broad; and [the space] between the lodges was five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate toward the house was one reed.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [every] little chamber [was] one reed long, and one reed broad; and between the little chambers [were] five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate within [was] one reed.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the chamber was equal in length to the reed, and equal in breadth to the reed; and the porch between the chambers six cubits; and the second chamber equal in breadth to the reed, and equal in length to the reed, and the porch five cubits.

pob.text: Then he measured the vestibule of the gate on the inside: one rod[a][b].

spob.text: Then he measured the entrance hall on the inner side of the gate. It measured one rod.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then he measured the portico of the gateway inside;
public_domain_references.web: He measured also the porch of the gate toward the house, one reed.
public_domain_references.asv: He measured also the porch of the gate toward the house, one reed.
public_domain_references.kjv: He measured also the porch of the gate within, one reed.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the third chamber equal in length to the reed, and equal in breadth to the reed.

pob.text: Then he measured the portico of the gate: eight cubits[a], and its side pillars two cubits[b]; and the portico of the gate was toward the temple.

spob.text: Then he measured the gate’s entrance hall. It measured about 12 feet (3.7 meters),[a] and its side pillars measured about 3 feet (0.9 meters).[b] The entrance hall was toward the temple.

public_domain_references.bsb: it was eight cubits deep, and its jambs were two cubits thick. And the portico of the gateway faced the temple.
public_domain_references.web: Then he measured the porch of the gate, eight cubits; and its posts, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was toward the house.
public_domain_references.asv: Then measured he the porch of the gate, eight cubits; and the posts thereof, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was toward the house.

pob.text: And the guardrooms of the gate facing east were three on this side and three on that side[a]; the three of them had one measure[b], and the side pillars had one measure on this side and on that side.

spob.text: The east-facing gate had three guardrooms on one side and three on the other.[a] Each set of three rooms had the same measurements. The side pillars on both sides also had the same measurements.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: There were three gate chambers on each side of the east gate, each with the same measurements, and the gateposts on either side also had the same measurements.
public_domain_references.web: The side rooms of the gate eastward were three on this side, and three on that side. The three of them were of one measure. The posts had one measure on this side and on that side.

public_domain_references.brenton: and the chambers of the gate of the chamber in front [were] three on one side and three on the other, and [there was] one measure to the three: [there was] one measure to the porches on this side and on that.

pob.text: Then he measured the width of the entrance of the gate: ten cubits[b][a], and the length of the gate: thirteen cubits.

spob.text: Then he measured the gate’s entrance. It was about 17½ feet (5.3 meters) wide, and the gate itself was about 22¾ feet (6.9 meters) long.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: And he measured the width of the gateway entrance to be ten cubits, and its length was thirteen cubits.

public_domain_references.asv: And he measured the breadth of the opening of the gate, ten cubits; and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits;
public_domain_references.kjv: And he measured the breadth of the entry of the gate, ten cubits; [and] the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he measured the breadth of the door of the gateway, ten cubits; and the breadth of the gateway thirteen cubits.

pob.text: And there was a barrier of one cubit in front of the side rooms[a], and a barrier of one cubit on the other side[b]; and each side room was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.

spob.text: On each side of the gateway, a barrier one cubit wide—about 21 inches—stood in front of the side rooms. Each room measured six cubits by six cubits, about 10½ feet by 10½ feet.

public_domain_references.bsb: In front of each gate chamber was a wall one cubit high, and the gate chambers were six cubits square.
public_domain_references.web: and a border before the lodges, one cubit on this side, and a border, one cubit on that side; and the side rooms, six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side.
public_domain_references.asv: and a border before the lodges, one cubit [on this side], and a border, one cubit on that side; and the lodges, six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side.
public_domain_references.kjv: The space also before the little chambers [was] one cubit [on this side], and the space [was] one cubit on that side: and the little chambers [were] six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the space before the chambers was narrowed to a cubit in front of the chambers on this side and on that side: and the chamber was six cubits this way, and six cubits that way.

pob.text: Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one guardroom to the roof of the other: twenty-five cubits wide[b][a], doorway opposite doorway.

spob.text: Then he measured across the gateway, from the roof of one guardroom[b] to the roof of the guardroom opposite it. The gateway was about 38 feet (11.5 meters) wide,[a] with the doorways facing each other.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one gate chamber to the roof of the opposite one; the distance was twenty-five cubits from doorway to doorway.
public_domain_references.web: He measured the gate from the roof of the one side room to the roof of the other, a width of twenty-five cubits, door against door.

public_domain_references.kjv: He measured then the gate from the roof of [one] little chamber to the roof of another: the breadth [was] five and twenty cubits, door against door.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he measured the gate from the wall of one chamber to the wall of the other chamber: the breadth was twenty-five cubits, the one gate over against the other gate.

pob.text: And he made the jambs sixty cubits, and to the jamb of the court the gate extended all around.

spob.text: He made the gateposts about ninety feet high. The gateway extended all the way around to the court’s gatepost.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Next he measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits high. The gateway extended around to the gatepost of the courtyard.
public_domain_references.web: He also made posts, sixty cubits; and the court reached to the posts, around the gate.

public_domain_references.kjv: He made also posts of threescore cubits, even unto the post of the court round about the gate.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the open space of the porch of the gate without, was twenty cubits to the chambers round about the gate.

pob.text: And from the front of the outer gateway to the front of the vestibule of the inner gate was fifty cubits[a][b][c].

spob.text: The distance from the front of the outer gateway[a] to the front of the entrance hall at the inner gate was fifty cubits—about 88 feet (27 meters).[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: And the distance from the entrance of the gateway to the far end of its inner portico was fifty cubits.
public_domain_references.web: From the forefront of the gate at the entrance to the forefront of the inner porch of the gate were fifty cubits.
public_domain_references.asv: And [from] the forefront of the gate at the entrance unto the forefront of the inner porch of the gate were fifty cubits.
public_domain_references.kjv: And from the face of the gate of the entrance unto the face of the porch of the inner gate [were] fifty cubits.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the open space of the gate without to the open space of the porch of the gate within was fifty cubits.

pob.text: And there were recessed windows toward the guardrooms and toward their side pillars[a], inward, all around the gate; and likewise for the porticos. And windows were all around on the inside[c][b], and on each pillar were palm-tree decorations.

spob.text: Recessed windows[a] faced inward toward the guardrooms and their side pillars all around the gateway. The entrance porches also had windows all around on the inside. Each pillar was decorated with palm-tree designs.

public_domain_references.bsb: The gate chambers and their side pillars had beveled windows all around the inside of the gateway. The porticos also had windows all around on the inside. Each side pillar was decorated with palm trees.

public_domain_references.kjv: And [there were] narrow windows to the little chambers, and to their posts within the gate round about, and likewise to the arches: and windows [were] round about inward: and upon [each] post [were] palm trees.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [there were] secret windows to the chambers, and to the porches within the gate of the court round about, and in the same manner windows to the porches round about within: and on the porch [there were] palm-trees on this side and on that side.

pob.text: Then he brought me into the outer court[a], and behold, there were chambers and a pavement made for the court all around, all around; thirty chambers were on the pavement.

spob.text: Then he brought me into the outer courtyard. I saw rooms and a paved area extending all the way around the courtyard. Thirty rooms faced the paved area.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the court. Thirty chambers faced the pavement,
public_domain_references.web: Then he brought me into the outer court. Behold, there were rooms and a pavement made for the court all around. Thirty rooms were on the pavement.

spob.text: The lower pavement lay beside the gates and extended along their length.[a]

pob.text: Then he measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court outside: one hundred cubits[b][a], to the east and to the north.

pob.text: As for the gate whose front faced north toward the outer court[a], he measured its length and its width.

pob.text: And a gate to the inner court was opposite the gate on the north and on the east[a]; and he measured from gate to gate one hundred cubits.

pob.text: Then he led me by way of the south[a], and behold, there was a gate facing south[b]. He measured its side pillars and its porch according to these measurements.

pob.text: And it had windows all around[a], and its porch also had windows all around, like these windows. The length was fifty cubits, and the width twenty-five cubits.

pob.text: And there was a gate to the inner court toward the south[a], and he measured from gate to gate toward the south: one hundred cubits.

spob.text: There was also a gate to the inner courtyard on the south side.[a] He measured southward from one gate to the other: 100 cubits.[b]

pob.text: Then he brought me into the inner court by way of the south gate[b][a], and he measured the south gate according to these measurements.

He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings[b], to make atonement for the house of Israel.

pob.text: Thus says the Lord GOD: In the first month[a], on the first day of the month, you shall take a bull from the herd without blemish, and you shall purify the sanctuary.

pob.text: And so you shall do on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or through simplicity[b][a]; thus you shall make atonement for the temple.

spob.text: Do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins without meaning to or who is naive or inexperienced.[a] In this way you will make atonement for the temple.

pob.text: In the first month[a], on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a feast of seven days[b]; unleavened bread shall be eaten.

spob.text: On the fourteenth day of the first month, you are to celebrate the Passover,[a] a seven-day festival. Bread made without yeast must be eaten.

pob.text: Thus says the Lord GOD: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall be shut during the six working days[a], but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

pob.text: And when the people of the land come before Yahweh at the appointed times[a], whoever enters by way of the north gate to worship shall go out by way of the south gate, and whoever enters by way of the south gate shall go out by way of the north gate. He shall not return by way of the gate through which he entered[c][b], but shall go out straight ahead.

spob.text: These are the city’s exits:[a] the north side is 4,500 units long.

public_domain_references.web: “These are the exits of the city: On the north side four thousand five hundred reeds by measure;
public_domain_references.asv: And these are the egresses of the city: On the north side four thousand and five hundred [reeds] by measure;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And these [are] the goings out of the city on the north side, four thousand and five hundred measures.
public_domain_references.brenton: And these are the goings out of the city northward, four thousand and five hundred by measure.

pob.text: And the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel: three gates on the north side—one gate of Reuben[a], one gate of Judah, one gate of Levi.

spob.text: The city’s gates will be named for the tribes of Israel. On the north side will be three gates: one named Reuben, one named Judah, and one named Levi.

public_domain_references.bsb: the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. On the north side there will be three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
public_domain_references.web: and the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
public_domain_references.asv: and the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the gates of the city [shall be] after the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward; one gate of Reuben, one gate of Judah, one gate of Levi.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the gates of the city [shall be] after the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward; the gate of Ruben, one, and the gate of Juda, one, and the gate of Levi, one.

pob.text: And on the east side[a], four thousand five hundred cubits, with three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.

spob.text: The east side will measure about 1.3 miles (2 kilometers) and have three gates: the Joseph Gate, the Benjamin Gate, and the Dan Gate—one of each.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: On the east side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
public_domain_references.web: “At the east side four thousand five hundred reeds, and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
public_domain_references.asv: And at the east side four thousand and five hundred [reeds], and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
public_domain_references.kjv: And at the east side four thousand and five hundred: and three gates; and one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of Dan.
public_domain_references.brenton: And eastward four thousand and five hundred: and three gates; the gate of Joseph, one, and the gate of Benjamin, one, and the gate of Dan, one.

pob.text: On the south side[a], 4,500 cubits by measure, with three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.

spob.text: The south side measures 4,500 cubits[a] and has three gates: one for Simeon, one for Issachar, and one for Zebulun.

public_domain_references.bsb: On the south side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
public_domain_references.web: “At the south side four thousand five hundred reeds by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
public_domain_references.asv: And at the south side four thousand and five hundred [reeds] by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
public_domain_references.kjv: And at the south side four thousand and five hundred measures: and three gates; one gate of Simeon, one gate of Issachar, one gate of Zebulun.
public_domain_references.brenton: And southward, four thousand and five hundred by measure: and three gates; the gate of Symeon, one, and the gate of Issachar, one, and the gate of Zabulon, one.

pob.text: On the west side[a], four thousand five hundred, with their three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali[b], one.

spob.text: The west side will measure 4,500 units and will have three gates: one named for Gad, one for Asher, and one for Naphtali.

public_domain_references.bsb: And on the west side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
public_domain_references.web: “At the west side four thousand five hundred reeds, with their three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
public_domain_references.asv: At the west side four thousand and five hundred [reeds], with their three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
public_domain_references.kjv: At the west side four thousand and five hundred, [with] their three gates; one gate of Gad, one gate of Asher, one gate of Naphtali.
public_domain_references.brenton: And westward, four thousand and five hundred by measure: [and] three gates; the gate of Gad, one, and the gate of Asser, one, and the gate of Nephthalim, one.

pob.text: All around shall be eighteen thousand[a], and the name of the city from that day on shall be, Yahweh Is There.

spob.text: The city will measure eighteen thousand all the way around. From that day on, its name will be Yahweh Is There.

public_domain_references.bsb: The perimeter of the city will be 18,000 cubits, and from that day on the name of the city will be: THE LORD IS THERE.”
public_domain_references.web: “It shall be eighteen thousand reeds in circumference; and the name of the city from that day shall be, ‘Yahweh is there.’
public_domain_references.asv: It shall be eighteen thousand [reeds] round about: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Jehovah is there.
public_domain_references.kjv: [It was] round about eighteen thousand [measures:] and the name of the city from [that] day [shall be], The LORD [is] there.
public_domain_references.brenton: The circumference, eighteen thousand [measures]: and the name of the city, from the day that it shall be finished, shall be the name thereof.
